open: [P18] build_menu_root.gd — THE ONE THING I UNMASKED AND CANNOT FIX. The world-hover inspection sheet stands down only while _card_up() is true, which is [P17]'s card_on_screen() -> LcnHudStage.card_visible(). With the card correctly off the stage during a fight, the sheet comes back and is now a 382x390 opaque panel over the city in every night frame (x 345..727, y 370..755 at 1920x1080 in artifacts/H3_ship/shots/assault.png and dusk.png), and it is drawn on top of [P22]'s waiting line, hiding two thirds of it. I cannot widen card_visible() to cover this: [P17]'s scrim reads the same function, and a scrim with no card is a dimmed city for no reason. The one-line fix is in _place_tooltip(): `if LcnWorldWatch.needs_watching(): tooltip.visible = false; return` — LcnWorldWatch is a public static rule in game/narrative/ written for exactly this kind of caller. This is the same mouse-follow branch E3 already flagged.

[P20] stats_root.gd:245 — THE AFTER-ACTION REPORT IS NEVER IN A SHIPPED FRAME. `if auto_report and not Harness.active: show_tab(TAB_NIGHT)`. The grade is computed in every run (artifacts/H3_ship/log.txt: 'night 2: HELD, BARELY — Night 2, 2 min 43 s · 25 killed · 2 buildings taken') and then not raised, because the raise is suppressed under the harness. So the screen that makes a player say one more day has never appeared in any artifact a critic has been handed. Nothing of mine covers it — the layer table puts STATS at 76 above NARRATIVE at 66, and LcnHudStage now withholds the card and therefore the scrim while any [P20] screen is open — but it cannot be photographed until [P20] or the integrator decides how a harness run should show it.

[P17] hud_layout.gd — the solver emits out["ticker"] only inside `if card_size != Vector2.ZERO`, so with the card off the stage [P22]'s feed had nowhere to go and the waiting line was drawn nowhere. LcnHudStage._fallback_ticker_slot() covers it from solved_rect(&"stage"), which is where the solver would have put it; if [P17] would rather emit the rectangle unconditionally, the fallback becomes dead code and should be deleted.

tests/d7/run_layout_audit.tscn DOES NOT FINISH — 560 s and still in its first cases, and it does the same on the parent commit (875a96b, my files reverted in a scratch copy, 400 s, same hang). check.sh caps a standalone suite at 240 s, so this suite is already timing out in the gate and its palette-x-sheet finding cannot currently be re-measured by anyone. Not mine and not caused by me, but somebody owns it.

[P13] tests/render/run_ground_frame.gd — the scrim ablation moved two of its bars. Against artifacts/H3_base it fails 4 of 10 (ARC 3.87x, NIGHT spread 0.040, NIGHT gradient 0.0078, LATE DAY 0.141); against artifacts/H3_ship it fails 2 of 10 — both NIGHT failures go green, because the night plain is no longer being dimmed 1.6x by [P22]'s scrim, and ARC gets worse (3.87x -> 2.37x) for the same reason: deep_night got legitimately brighter while midday did not move. [P13]'s night bars were calibrated on frames that had a narrative scrim in them. Recalibrate against a scrim-free night or make the night darker for real; do not move the bar to make the red go away.

The rule takes the card off the stage for the WHOLE night, not only while bodies are on the map — that is the brief's 'it comes back when the night is over', and it is what dusk, deep_night and second_dusk measure. Five of eleven beats of first_night now have no card. The other six do (47-62% plated), and run_fight_frames.gd fails if that ever stops being true. If a designer wants the card back at, say, deep night with nothing alive, the single knob is LcnWorldWatch.watch()'s `if active: return Watch.ASSAULT` rung.
